view.name: Workspace Tasks
description: Manage and run tasks in your workspace
config.group.general.title: General
config.group.discovery.title: Task Discovery
config.group.display.title: Display & Interaction
config.group.execution.title: Task Execution
config.group.environment.title: Environment
config.group.taskEnv.title: Environment Variables
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.env: Global environment variables applied to all tasks.
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.env.markdo: Key-value pairs that are merged into every task's environment. Values from higher-precedence sources override these. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/environment-variables.html#workspacetasksenvvarsenv)
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.envFiles: One or more .env files loaded for all tasks (string, string array, or include/exclude glob object).
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.envFiles.m: Paths/globs resolved relative to the workspace root. Glob expansions are sorted alphabetically. Supports a single path, an ordered array, or `{ include, exclude }` object. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/environment-variables.html#workspacetasksenvvarsenvfiles)
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.secretFile: One or more .secret files loaded for all tasks. Values never trigger secret-pattern warnings.

Same format as `workspaceTasks.envVars.envFiles`. Files with a `.secret` extension are treated as explicitly secret — keys are injected without triggering the secret-name warning. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/environment-variables.html#workspacetasksenvvarssecretfiles)
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.secretPatt: Key-name patterns that trigger a warning when a matching variable is declared in a non-secret source (e.g. env block or .env file).

Supports glob-style wildcard patterns (e.g. `*_TOKEN`). Variables whose names match these patterns but originate from a `.secret` file or VS Code SecretStorage are **never** warned about. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/environment-variables.html#workspacetasksenvvarssecretfiles)
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.warnIfGitT: When enabled, emits a warning in the Problems panel for any file listed in envFiles or secretFiles that is tracked by git.

When `true`, Workspace Tasks checks all files resolved from `workspaceTasks.envVars.envFiles` and `workspaceTasks.envVars.secretFiles` against git and reports a warning in the Problems panel for any file that is tracked. Files containing environment variables or secrets should be added to `.gitignore` to avoid accidentally committing sensitive data. Set to `false` to disable this check entirely. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/environment-variables.html#workspacetasksenvvarswarnifgittracked)
config.workspaceTasks.secrets.showEmptyG: When enabled, the Secrets group is always shown in the treeview even when no secrets are stored.

When `true`, the **Secrets** group is always visible in the Workspace Tasks treeview, even when VS Code SecretStorage contains no secrets. This provides a consistent treeview layout and makes it easier to discover the secrets feature. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/general/secrets.html#workspacetaskssecretsshowemptygroup)
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.taskEnv: Per-task environment rules — inject env vars and secrets into any discovered task by matching on task name, type, source file, and/or workspace folder.
config.workspaceTasks.envVars.taskEnv.ma: Each rule has a `match` object (AND logic) and optional `env`, `envFiles`, `secretFiles`, and `secrets` properties. All matching rules are applied in array order; later rules override earlier rules per key. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/environment-variables.html#workspacetasksenvvarstaskenv)
command.purgeInvalidCompoundTasks: Purge Invalid Compound Tasks from Storage
config.workspaceTasks.debug: Enable debug logging for Workspace Tasks
config.workspaceTasks.debug.markdown: When enabled, the extension will output detailed debug logs to the WorkspaceTasks Output Channel. This can help with troubleshooting issues. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/general/debugging#workspacetasksdebug)
config.workspaceTasks.task.guidedArgInpu: When enabled, running script tasks with arguments will attempt to discover the script's parameters and show guided input prompts. Supported for PowerShell (`.ps1`) via `Get-Help` (with static `param()` block parsing as fallback), Python (`.py`) scripts using `argparse`, and Node.js (`.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`) scripts using `argparse` or `parseArgs` (`node:util` and `@pkgjs/parseargs`). Falls back to free-text input when parameters cannot be detected

When enabled, running script tasks with arguments will attempt to discover the script's parameters and show guided input prompts. Supported for PowerShell (.ps1) via Get-Help (with static param() block parsing as fallback), Python (.py) scripts using argparse, and Node.js (.js/.mjs/.cjs) scripts using argparse or parseArgs (node:util and @pkgjs/parseargs). Falls back to free-text input when parameters cannot be detected
config.workspaceTasks.task.actionBar: Select which items should be shown in the task action bar for each task. This allows you to customize the actions available for tasks in the workspace. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-action.html#workspacetaskstaskactionbar)
config.workspaceTasks.autoRefresh: Automatically refresh tasks when changes are detected
config.workspaceTasks.autoRefresh.descri: Automatically refresh tasks when changes are detected
config.workspaceTasks.autoRefresh.markdo: When enabled, the extension will automatically refresh the task list whenever changes are detected in the workspace.
config.workspaceTasks.enabledTaskTypes.d: Select the types of tasks that the extension should support and display in the task list.
config.workspaceTasks.enabledTaskTypes.m: Choose the task types (e.g., npm, script, makefile) that the extension will recognize and show in the task list. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/task-types/#enabling--disabling-task-types)
config.workspaceTasks.enabledTaskTypePat: Glob patterns matched against **internal task type names** (e.g. `dockerfile`, `justfile`) to **enable**. When non-empty, acts as a whitelist — only matching types are shown. `disabledTaskTypePatterns` takes precedence. Uses [micromatch](https://github.com/micromatch/micromatch) glob syntax. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-discovery/discovery#workspacetasksenabledtasktypepatterns)
config.workspaceTasks.disabledTaskTypePa: Glob patterns matched against **internal task type names** (e.g. `dockerfile`, `justfile`) to **disable**. Always takes precedence over `enabledTaskTypePatterns` and `enabledTaskTypes`. Uses [micromatch](https://github.com/micromatch/micromatch) glob syntax. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-discovery/discovery#workspacetasksdisabledtasktypepatterns)
config.workspaceTasks.shellEnabledTaskTy: Enable support for specific shell script types. This allows the extension to recognize and run tasks defined in these shell scripts. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/shell-script.html#workspacetasksshellenabledtasktypes)
config.workspaceTasks.task.forceStopMeth: Controls how a task is force-stopped when clicking **Stop** a second time (after the initial SIGINT was sent). `ask` (the default) shows a quick-pick so you can choose the signal interactively. `SIGINT` sends a second interrupt, `SIGTERM` requests a graceful exit, and `SIGKILL` immediately kills the process. When possible the terminal panel is preserved regardless of the chosen signal. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-execution/tasks#workspacetaskstaskforcestopmethod)
Show a quick-pick to choose the signal interactively
config.workspaceTasks.task.stopCompoundD: When enabled, stopping a compound Visual Studio Code task from the Workspace Tasks stop action will also stop any currently running dependency tasks referenced by `dependsOn`. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-execution/tasks#workspacetaskstaskstopcompounddependencies)
config.workspaceTasks.task.confirmPatter: Array of strings (treated as regular expressions, case-insensitive) matched against task labels. Tasks whose labels match any pattern will prompt for confirmation before running. Example: `["deploy.*", "db:drop", "terraform apply"]`. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-execution/tasks.html#workspacetaskstaskconfirmpatterns)
config.workspaceTasks.task.iconType: Choose the Icon Type for Tasks
config.workspaceTasks.task.iconType.mark: Select the type of icon to display for tasks. Options include predefined icons or custom icons specified by the user. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-icon.html#workspacetaskstaskicontype)
config.workspaceTasks.task.iconTypeCusto: Specify a custom icon for the task. This can be a path to an png or svg file, or it can be a [ThemeIcon](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/icons-in-labels) in the format `$(iconName)`. `workspaceTasks.task.iconType` must be set to `custom` for this to take effect. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-icon.html#workspacetaskstaskicontypecustom)
config.workspaceTasks.task.presentationO: Configure how task output is presented in the user interface. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-presentation.html#workspacetaskstaskpresentationoptions)
Controls if the task panel is used for this task only (dedicated), shared between tasks (shared) or if a new panel is created on every task execution (new).
Controls whether the task output is revealed in the user interface.
Controls whether the panel showing the task output is taking focus.
Controls whether the command associated with the task is echoed in the user interface.

Controls whether the terminal is closed after executing the task. When set to false (the default), the terminal panel remains open after the task ends — including when the task is force-stopped — so you can review the last output.
Controls whether the terminal is cleared before executing the task.
config.workspaceTasks.task.singleClickAc: Action to perform when a task is single-clicked.  `run` - Run the task  `open` - Open the task  `none` - Do nothing. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-display.html#workspacetaskstasksingleclickaction)
config.workspaceTasks.task.doubleClickAc: Action to perform when a task is double-clicked.  `run` - Run the task  `open` - Open the task  `none` - Do nothing. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-display.html#workspacetaskstaskdoubleclickaction)
config.workspaceTasks.task.statusResetDe: The delay in **milliseconds** before resetting the task icon back to its original state after execution. Set to `0` to reset immediately. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-display.html#workspacetaskstaskstatusresetdelay)
config.workspaceTasks.shellAdditionalExt: Additional File Extensions for Shell Tasks

Add extra file extensions (beyond the default ones) that should be treated as shell tasks. Use a key-value format where the key is a file extension without the leading dot (e.g., `myscript`) and the value is the path to the shell interpreter (e.g., `/usr/local/bin/myshell`). This allows you to run custom script files as tasks within the extension. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/shell-script.html#workspacetasksshellenabledtasktypes)
config.workspaceTasks.shellPaths.markdow: Specify custom paths for shell interpreters. Use a key-value format where the key is the shell type (e.g., `bash`, `pwsh`) and the value is the path to the shell executable (e.g., `/usr/local/bin/bash`). This allows you to customize which shell interpreters are used for running shell tasks. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/shell-script.html#workspacetasksshellpaths)
config.workspaceTasks.tasks.sortingEnabl: When enabled, tasks will be sorted alphabetically within their groups. Otherwise, tasks will be displayed in the order they are discovered. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/display-interaction/tasks.html#workspacetaskstaskssortingenabled)
config.workspaceTasks.groups.useParentFo: Group tasks by their parent folder.

When enabled, tasks will be grouped based on their parent folder in addition to other grouping rules. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-grouping.html#workspacetasksgroupsuseparentfolder)
config.workspaceTasks.groups.taskSeparat: Separator used to split task name into groups.

Separator used to split task name into groups. For example, a task named `build:frontend` with a separator of `:` would be grouped under `build`. An empty string means no grouping will be applied. To use a regular expression as the separator, enable `workspaceTasks.groups.taskSeparatorIsRegex`. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-grouping.html#workspacetasksgroupstaskseparator)
When enabled, the Task Separator value is treated as a JavaScript regular expression pattern.

When enabled, the `workspaceTasks.groups.taskSeparator` value is compiled as a JavaScript regular-expression pattern instead of a plain string. Only the first match per grouping level is consumed (the algorithm is recursive). Regex flags (e.g. case-insensitive `i`) are not supported in this iteration. If the pattern is invalid, the extension falls back to plain-string matching and shows a warning. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-grouping.html#workspacetasksgroupstaskseparatorisregex)
config.workspaceTasks.exclude.descriptio: Glob patterns to exclude from tasks.
config.workspaceTasks.exclude.markdown: Glob patterns to exclude from tasks. For example, to ignore all tasks in `sample` folders, add `**/sample/**`. Note that the patterns follow the [glob syntax](https://github.com/micromatch/glob). `**/node_modules/**` and `**/.git/**` are always ignored. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/general.html#workspacetasksexclude)
config.workspaceTasks.groups.enabled.des: Group tasks by type, folder, and custom separator.
config.workspaceTasks.groups.enabled.mar: When enabled, tasks will be grouped based on the specified separator and other grouping rules. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-grouping.html#workspacetasksgroupsenabled)
config.workspaceTasks.groups.recentTasks: When enabled, recent tasks will be grouped based on the specified separator and other grouping rules. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-grouping.html#workspacetasksgroupsrecenttasksenabled)
config.workspaceTasks.groups.justfile.en: When enabled, justfile recipes decorated with [group('name')] are shown as collapsible group nodes in the task tree.
When enabled, justfile recipes decorated with `[group('name')]` are shown as collapsible group nodes in the task tree. Requires just ≥ 1.13.0. Defaults to `false`.
config.workspaceTasks.groups.compoundTas: When enabled, compound tasks (previously called 'Queues') will be grouped together in the task view. Otherwise, each compound task will be shown at the root level of the task view. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/features/task-queues.html#vscode-compound-tasks-in-the-compound-tasks-group)
config.workspaceTasks.groups.expanded.ma: Control which groups are expanded by default. You can specify favorites, compound tasks, and recent tasks. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-grouping.html#workspacetasksgroupsexpanded)
config.workspaceTasks.recentTasks.maxIte: Maximum number of recent tasks to display.

Maximum number of recent tasks to display in the Recent Tasks group. Once the limit is reached, the oldest tasks will drop off the list. Set to 0 to disable the Recent Tasks group. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/features/favorites.html#workspacetasksrecenttasksmaxitems)
config.workspaceTasks.metrics.scope.desc: Where task execution metrics are stored.
config.workspaceTasks.metrics.scope.mark: Controls where task execution metrics are persisted. `workspace` stores metrics per-workspace, `global` stores them across all workspaces, `both` writes to both stores, and `disabled` turns off metrics collection entirely. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/metrics.html#workspacetasksmetricsscope)
config.workspaceTasks.metrics.scope.glob: Store metrics in global state (shared across workspaces)
config.workspaceTasks.metrics.scope.both: Write metrics to both workspace and global state
config.workspaceTasks.metrics.maxDuratio: Maximum number of recent task duration samples to retain for statistics.

The number of most-recent task duration samples (in ms) to keep per task for computing median, p95, and trend statistics. Must be between 10 and 1000. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/metrics.html#workspacetasksmetricsmaxdurationsamples)
config.workspaceTasks.metrics.retentionD: Number of days to retain task metrics. Set to 0 for no limit.

Task metrics for tasks that have not run within this many days will be pruned when the extension starts. Set to `0` (the default) to keep metrics indefinitely. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/metrics.html#workspacetasksmetricsretentiondays)
config.workspaceTasks.history.maxPersist: Maximum number of task execution records to persist per workspace. Oldest records are pruned when the cap is exceeded.

Controls how many task execution records are kept in VS Code's workspace state (fast read cache). Oldest records by start time are dropped when the cap is exceeded. The NDJSON archive file (`.vscode/task-history.ndjson`) is subject only to `retentionDays`. Must be between 10 and 2000. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/features/task-history.html#persistence)
config.workspaceTasks.history.retentionD: Number of days to retain persisted task history. Set to 0 for no limit.

Task history records older than this many days are pruned from both the workspace state cache and the NDJSON archive when the extension starts. Set to `0` (the default) to keep history indefinitely. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/features/task-history.html#persistence)
config.workspaceTasks.compoundTasks.defa: Specify the default execution type for compound tasks (previously called 'Queues'). Options are 'sequential' or 'parallel'. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-execution/compound-tasks.html#workspacetaskscompoundtasksdefaultexecutiontype)
config.workspaceTasks.compoundTasks.incl: Include Visual Studio Code Compound Tasks

When enabled along with `workspaceTasks.groups.compoundTasks.enabled`, compound tasks defined in Visual Studio Code (using `type: 'compound'` in `tasks.json`) will be included in the `Compound Tasks` group. They will still be defined in the normal tree structure based on their `group` and `label` even if this setting is disabled. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/features/task-queues.html#vscode-compound-tasks-in-the-compound-tasks-group)
config.workspaceTasks.taskDiscovery.fetc: Specify the fetch depth when discovering tasks from within the workspace. A value of `null` means full fetch, while a positive integer limits the depth of the fetch operation. This can help improve performance when working with large repositories. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/task-types/#performance-task-discovery-depth)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ac: Act allows you to run GitHub Actions locally. Specify the path to the [Act](https://github.com/nektos/act) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `act`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathact)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ci: Specify the path to the [CircleCI CLI](https://circleci.com/docs/guides/toolkit/local-cli/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `circleci`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, `~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/application-paths/circleci.html)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.bi: Specify the path to the [pipeline-runner](https://github.com/bitbucket-pipeline-runner/pipeline-runner) executable used to run Bitbucket Pipelines locally.
workspaceTasks.act.envFile: Path to Act environment variables file
workspaceTasks.act.envFile.markdown: Specify the path to a .env file containing environment variables for Act. This file will be used to provide environment variable values when running GitHub Actions locally with Act. For examples of the file format see the [Act documentation](https://nektosact.com/usage/index.html#envsecrets-files-structure). [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/github-actions.html#workspacetasksactenvfile)
workspaceTasks.act.secretsFile.markdown: Specify the path to a .env file containing secrets for Act. This file will be used to provide secret values when running GitHub Actions locally with Act. For examples of the file format see the [Act documentation](https://nektosact.com/usage/index.html#envsecrets-files-structure). [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/github-actions.html#workspacetasksactsecretsfile)
workspaceTasks.act.variables.markdown: Variables to pass to 'act'. Each key-value pair represents a variable name and its corresponding value. These variables will be made available to the GitHub Actions workflows when running locally with Act. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/application-paths/act#workspacetasksactvariables)
workspaceTasks.act.variablesFile.markdow: Path to the variables file for `act`. The file format is the same as `.env` file format. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/github-actions.html#workspacetasksactvariablesfile)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.an: Specify the path to the Ant executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `ant`, `.bat` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathant)
config.workspaceTasks.ant.ansicon.enable: When enabled, ANSICON will be used for Ant tasks to provide colored output in the terminal. This requires that the `workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ansicon` setting is configured with the path to the ANSICON executable. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/application-paths/ant.html#workspacetasksantansiconenabled)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.an: Specify the path to the ANSICON executable. This is used to enable colored output for Ant tasks in the terminal. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathansicon)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ms: Specify the path to the MSBuild executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `msbuild`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathmsbuild)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.co: Specify the path to the [Composer](https://getcomposer.org/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `composer`, `.bat` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathcomposer)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.gr: Specify the path to the [Gradle](https://gradle.org/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `gradle`, `.bat` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathgradle)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ju: Specify the path to the [Just](https://just.systems/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `just`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathjust)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.pi: Specify the path to the [Pipenv](https://pipenv.pypa.io/en/latest/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `pipenv`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathpipenv)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.po: Path to Poe the Poet executable

Specify the path to the [Poe the Poet](https://poethepoet.natn.io/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `poe`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/application-paths/#workspacetasksapplicationpathpoe)

Specify the path to the [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `poetry`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/application-paths/#workspacetasksapplicationpathpoetry)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ma: Specify the path to the Make executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `make`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathmake)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ra: Specify the path to the [Rake](https://ruby.github.io/rake/) executable. On all platforms, '~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/application-paths/#workspacetasksapplicationpathrake)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.ta: Specify the path to the [Task](https://taskfile.dev/) executable. On Windows, if the path ends with `task`, `.exe` will be appended automatically. On all platforms, `~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/application-path.html#workspacetasksapplicationpathtask)
config.workspaceTasks.applicationPath.gi: Specify the path to the [gitlab-ci-local](https://github.com/firecow/gitlab-ci-local) executable. On all platforms, `~/` will be expanded to the user's home directory. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/environment/application-paths/gitlab-ci-local.html)
config.workspaceTasks.additionalFilePatt: Additional glob patterns for any file-based task provider. Keys use task type config names such as `make`, `just`, `npm`, `taskfile`, `gitlab-ci`, and `circleci`. Invalid keys are ignored. Example: `{ "make": ["**/*.mk"] }`. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/configuration/task-discovery/discovery.html#workspacetasksadditionalfilepatterns)
config.workspaceTasks.gitlabCiLocal.addi: Deprecated: use `workspaceTasks.additionalFilePatterns.gitlab-ci` instead. Additional glob patterns for discovering `.gitlab-ci.yml` files with non-standard names or locations. Merged with the built-in `**/.gitlab-ci.yml` pattern. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/task-types/gitlab-ci.html#custom-file-patterns)
config.workspaceTasks.gitlabCiLocal.vari: Path to a YAML file containing CI/CD variables passed to `gitlab-ci-local` via `--variables-file`. [Read More](https://camalot.github.io/vscode-workspace-tasks/task-types/gitlab-ci.html#variables)
